name: OpenWork v0.18.60
body:
## Move older OpenWork installs to OpenCode v2 in the background

- **Older installs move to OpenCode v2 in the background.** Existing installs still using OpenCode v1 are moved over automatically, with a backup made first so your chats are kept. Windows installers also carry less duplicate engine data, and Windows can identify OpenWork's signed app files.
- **Computer use is more capable and predictable.** For Mac users, the agent can script apps directly and keeps working while you use your computer; Take over and Stop return control, and Continue resumes the task. Workbot can also script supported desktop apps. Browser pages keep a steady desktop, tablet, or phone size while the panel changes, and forms take fewer steps. When available, you can dictate into OpenWork or Workbot.
- **Chat can work with more of your existing tasks and connections.** Type `#` to add another task as context, ask the agent to create or move sidebar groups, and find connected actions with everyday wording. You can finish or repair an API-key connection in chat without sharing the key with the agent, and OpenWork Cloud tools work again in older desktop versions.
- **Documents and first launches are more dependable.** Closing an edited document now gives clear save, discard, or cancel choices, and reloading or reopening it preserves your editing session and unsaved work. Workbot can open a requested document beside chat, explain why a file could not open, and show or rebuild a computer that will not connect. Fresh desktop installs can load built-in tools even if the package registry is unavailable; slow Windows sign-in and first launch no longer hide recovery options.
- **For admins: team and organization controls are clearer.** Platform administrators can manage feature access per organization member and, when enabled, grant organizations Web access or extra Free Auto usage. Admins can finish connector setup after a check fails, remove connectors, and save team-role changes reliably; Workbot settings show one default model and its availability. When available, Workbot can guide eligible people from free Auto to paid Luna without losing the conversation.
- **Website visitors can find practical AI governance guidance.** The expanded enterprise pages explain governing employee AI and planning an OpenWork rollout.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.59...v0.18.60)

*Windows installers are signed using Microsoft Artifact Signing.*


## Known open fixes
Shipped without (decided by Ben, 2026-10-22: none is a regression introduced since v0.18.59; all are older fork PRs still in review): #6043, #5915, #5749, #5613, #4680, #4215, #4061, #4009, #4007, #4005, #3970, #3903, #3781, #3595, #3414, #3413. No PR opened since v0.18.59 matched the release fix filter.

name: v7.0.1
body:
This release retunes brainstorming after its rebuild in v7.0.0. Many of you told us, rightly, that the new default questions got annoying fast and felt formulaic. Brainstorming now digs for context before it asks anything, and tries to ask better questions. We expect to keep tuning it, but we think it's better than it was.

It also trims three long skills so they better survive compaction on Claude Code, and changes the issue and PR templates to ask for a summary written by a human.

### Brainstorming

- **It digs for context first.** In an existing project, or when you point it at a spec, plan, or files, it reads them before its first message and doesn't ask what they already answer. (#2560)
- **It tries to ask better questions.** v7.0.0 opened every session the same way: an offer to skip the questions, then a generic question about "the moment you wished this existed." Now, when you've already said what you want, it plays your request back with what it found in the project and asks about the one thing still open. Later questions build on your answers and on what it found, and say what the answer would change. (#2560, #2571)
- **It offers to skip the questions only when it started on its own.** If you asked for brainstorming by name or with `/brainstorming`, it no longer offers to skip it. (#2560)
- **It lays out the approaches and writes a design doc before building.** It presents two or three ways to build the thing, recommends one, and asks you to pick. Then it writes a design doc, a short one for a small change, and builds nothing until you approve it. Some of you saw it skip the doc and start building; in one of our test scenarios, it skipped the doc without asking in 24 of 24 runs before this change and 3 of 24 after. (#2571)

Thanks to @mbcrawfo for opening #2530, and to @katyatitkova, @ertra, @blorenz, @Biomaj, @fsalum, @technicalpickles, @orochi235, @alexxburg, @fcavalieri, @CelesteCunha, and @zzzzz9999 for the reports, transcripts, and testing there.

If brainstorming's questions in 7.0.1 still don't feel right, please comment on #2530. Examples help most: what you asked, what it asked back, and what you wish it had asked.

### Skills better survive compaction on Claude Code

After a compaction, Claude Code re-attaches each skill cut off at 20,000 characters, so anything past that point is gone for the rest of the session. In one reported session, subagent-driven development lost its five-round limit and ran 18 fix rounds on one task. Thanks @dan-1492 for the report. (#2481)

- **`subagent-driven-development`** moves the fix loop, final review, report handling, resuming, preflight, batching, and cannot-verify guidance into `references/`. It reads each file from disk at the step that needs it. (#2565)
- **`writing-skills`** moves its supporting docs, the SKILL.md template and discovery guidance, bulletproofing, and flowchart conventions into `references/`. (#2564)
- **`executing-plans`** drops its Example Workflow, which repeated rules stated above it. (#2563)
- `tests/skill-size/test-skill-size.sh` fails when any `SKILL.md` reaches 20,000 bytes. (#2565)

### Contributing

- **Issue and PR templates now ask who is filing and what their human partner asked for, plus a summary of under 200 words written by a human.** The bug report also asks how you confirmed the problem doesn't happen without Superpowers. (#2569)
- **We don't accept agent-written PRs that fix someone else's issue unless a maintainer asked for one.** If your human partner hit the same problem, add their report to the existing issue. The PR template, `AGENTS.md`, and the README say so. (#2569)
- **`diagnosing-superpowers` adds the same two sections to the issues it drafts** and won't file one while the summary is a placeholder. Its prefilled link now opens the Bug Report template; we removed the Session Diagnosis Report template. (#2569)

name: v5.1.41
body:
**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.21-1: engine hosts start faster and idle far more quietly, Claude subscriptions use the native 1M context again, and desktop threads are lighter ([#10740](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10740)).** A new engine host starts about 0.1 s faster, and an idle engine host wakes 405 times per 90 s instead of 1,106. Current Claude subscription models (Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7 and later) get their native 1M window back without asking for extra usage, and the Claude subscription lane runs Claude Code 2.1.306. Each desktop thread's engine supervisor starts from its own small program instead of the whole CLI, and messages and tool cards no longer keep duplicate copies (about 640 bytes per message and 2 KB per tool card). Models that models.dev marks deprecated stay available, labeled deprecated, instead of disappearing (GitHub Copilot Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4, Baseten Kimi K2 and others), and the model catalog is refreshed; some models get updated thinking levels (for example Nemotron 3 Ultra: off is now none). A message that was already delivered no longer stays listed under Steering, and with several accounts for one provider a usage limit stops failing turns once its reset has passed; a quota failure now says when it resets.

**Memory sync refuses signatures under weak Ed25519 keys.** Bun's WebCrypto accepts a signature made under a small-order public key, such as the identity key, for any message. The sync client now checks every key and signature it verifies itself, and refuses any keyring record that would bring a weak or malformed signing key into the account's keyring, including keys that appear only inside a fork-resolution's evidence. ([#10743](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10743), fixes [#10742](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10742))

**Outside full access, computer use asks before it acts on your screen as a whole.** Clicks, typing, key presses, scrolling, drags, pointer moves and holds aimed at the desktop or a display land on your real pointer and frontmost app, so they now need the same "Allow foreground computer control?" approval as foreground input; without it they fail with `ControlRequired` and nothing is sent. Input to one window in the background still needs no approval, and full access keeps working without a prompt, headless runs included. The macOS background check no longer moves your pointer back after you moved it, and a stopped session stays stopped when the desktop engine restarts. ([#10788](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10788), [#10790](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10790))

**OmO counts how often you had to repeat a standing instruction ([#10780](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10780), [#10786](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10786)).** Rules like "never filter the monitor output" now live in `system/agreements.md` with a count. When you correct the agent on something an agreement already covers, the count goes up; after the third time (`memory.agreements.needs_human_threshold`) the agent is told the rule keeps being broken and you see a notice. `/agreements` lists them and lets you add your own, acknowledge one, or drop one; the agreements you add can only be changed by you. The design is inspired by dinobot by roach (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0); no dinobot code was used.

**The launcher deletes a legacy `~/.omo/credentials.json` left by an intermediate sign-in build.** The file held the device's private keys and account refresh material in plaintext, sometimes world-readable; upgrading removes it. Only the exact legacy shape is removed. ([#10697](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10697), [#10698](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10698))

**Report a problem from inside OmO ([#10546](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10546)).** `/feedback` (or `/bug`) sends a bug report or an idea to the OmO team in one step: your description plus your account, this device, versions, this conversation's recent messages, recent logs and your settings. Passwords, keys and tokens are removed first with the same redactor `/share` uses, your memory is never sent, and `OMO_DISABLE_FEEDBACK=1` saves the report as a local file instead of uploading it. The desktop app's Report a problem dialog uses the same report.

**A DAG node whose child dies on infrastructure is retried instead of taking its whole branch down.** When a mass-ulw node's child stops answering its heartbeats or loses its host session, the node is now retried automatically, at most twice, with a backoff. Its dependents are skipped only if the retries fail too. Before, one starved wave failed and every later node was skipped (an overloaded machine skipped 54 of 61 nodes). Task failures and cancelled nodes behave as before, and the TUI and the desktop app share this behaviour ([#10605](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10605), [#10616](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10616)).

**Stopping a language server on Windows no longer raises a stray broken-pipe error.** When an LSP server's pipe closed while OmO was shutting the server down, Windows could report the failed write after cleanup had already let go of it, and the EPIPE escaped as an unhandled error. Every pipe of a spawned language server now keeps an error handler for its whole life, so the failure is logged as ignored cleanup noise ([#9601](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9601), [#10725](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10725)).

**The frontend skill now covers HTML reports, figures and slides, and its stripe check catches square callouts.** The skill now loads for any HTML, CSS or SVG made for visual output (a report printed to PDF, a figure, a diagram, a slide, an image for Notion or Slack), not only web UI. Its `check-accent-stripes.ts` linter fails a coloured bar along one side of a box whether the box is rounded or square, and a 2px-or-wider accent outline on a rounded card. Neutral hairlines, table rules, a blockquote's neutral rule, focus rings and input validation states stay allowed. The `visualize` skill runs the linter on every page before previewing or showing it ([#10774](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10774), [#10776](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10776)).

**`ulw-research` shows its report inline and checks a visual reproduction against the source ([#10812](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10812)).** When the host can show an HTML page in the thread (`show_html_page`, `html_render`), the run ends with the report there, before the file paths, on every tier and even when the research was shortened; a built app or 3D scene shown inline no longer stands in for it. When the ask is to recreate something visual, such as a clip rebuilt in 3D, the run puts real frames of the source next to its own output at the same moments, writes down what differs, fixes the biggest gaps, and shows the side-by-side pairs in the report.


### Changed

- Combine macOS root-test shards and Codex/Senpi compatibility into one runner job, preserving their existing check names through Ubuntu status jobs. Full-matrix CI now requests two macOS runners per head instead of five, including unchanged native binary parity; fast paths skip the combined allocation ([#10804](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10804)).

- CI: pull requests run the macOS and Windows legs only when a platform-specific path changes: any path a macOS/Windows-only CI step names (derived from the workflow), native crates, the launcher and platform packaging, the Windows Git Bash runtime, the Codex installer, platform-named sources, and the CI workflows. Pushes to `dev` and merge groups still run every OS, and the `run-full-ci` label forces the full matrix on a pull request ([#10856](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10856)). ([#10859](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10859))

name: CC Switch v4.0.18
body:
# CC Switch v4.0.18

本版本新增对 Antigravity CLI（agy）的支持，它是 CC Switch 管理的第 11 个应用。你可以为 agy 添加官方登录卡和第三方 API Key 卡。**注意：Antigravity 的供应商只在从 CC Switch 卡片「使用此供应商打开终端」启动的 agy 里生效**，在其他终端里直接运行 `agy` 不会用到它；MCP、Skills 和提示词同步给 agy，会话可以浏览和恢复，用量从会话日志导入；「应用」页可以安装、升级、卸载 agy。macOS 上，授权中心还能管理多个 Antigravity 账号：一键切换 agy 的登录，查看每个账号的额度，把官方卡绑定到某个账号。另外，Windows 上的应用内更新不会再因为文件被占用而重启电脑，MSI 安装时可以选择不创建桌面快捷方式；页头改为在应用名旁用小徽章显示实际的连接。还修复了 macOS 上并发请求多时路由因文件句柄耗尽而失败、从访达启动时「重启 Codex 守护进程」报 `env: node`、Claude Code 会话用 `/cd` 换目录后仍归在旧项目下、Windows 上打开终端后一直转圈直到关掉终端窗口、Codex 未使用的额度窗口显示倒计时、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 没有计价等问题。4.0 完整的更新内容请见 [v4.0 发布说明](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.4-zh.md)。

**[English →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.18-en.md) | [日本語版 →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.18-ja.md)**

---

## 新增

### Antigravity CLI（agy）

Google 的 Antigravity CLI（命令是 `agy`）现在是一个独立的应用，有自己的供应商、MCP、Skills、提示词、会话和用量，和 Gemini CLI 分开管理（[#8268](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8268)、[#2959](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/2959)）。

> **⚠️ Antigravity 的供应商必须从 CC Switch 以终端启动才生效。** 和其他应用不同，CC Switch 不改 agy 自己的设置文件，所以 Antigravity 的卡片没有「切换」，也没有「使用中」。要用哪张卡，就点那张卡上的「使用此供应商打开终端」，在弹出的终端里运行的 agy 才会用这家供应商；在其他终端里直接运行 `agy`，用的仍是 agy 自己的 Google 登录和设置。（macOS 上在授权中心切换账号是例外：它改的是 agy 的全局登录，见下一节。）

- **两种供应商卡。** 官方登录卡用 agy 自己的 Google 登录，打开终端时用卡上选的模型启动 agy，只对这次会话生效；第三方卡填兼容 Gemini API 的地址和 Key，地址留空用 Google 默认的 API，Key 和地址只交给这个终端里的 agy，不写进 agy 的配置和 shell 启动文件（启动用的临时文件会自动删除）。模型列表来自 agy 自带的模型目录，填的是 agy 认得的显示名称。
- **MCP、Skills、提示词。** 同步到 `~/.gemini/config`，这是 agy 的全局定制目录，可能和同一台电脑上的 Antigravity IDE 共用。第三方卡启动的 agy 同样能用这些 MCP、Skills 和提示词。
- **会话。** 可以浏览 agy 和 Antigravity IDE 的会话，只显示你输入的内容，不显示 agy 自己附加的上下文；第三方卡启动的会话也能找到，并用同一张卡恢复。
- **用量。** 从会话日志导入（包括 Antigravity IDE 的会话），按每轮选择的模型记账，费用按价格表里对应模型的 API 价格估算。
- **官方额度。** 在官方卡上开启额度查询后，显示 Gemini 和 Claude/GPT 两组额度，每组有 5 小时和每周两个窗口；卡片上每组只显示剩得少的那个窗口，点开下拉可以看全部四个窗口和各自的重置时间。
- **「应用」页管理 agy。** 用官方安装脚本安装，用 `agy update` 升级（Homebrew 安装的也一样），可以卸载。
- 深链接也可以导入 agy 的供应商、MCP 和提示词。

### 授权中心管理多个 Antigravity 账号（macOS）

agy 同时只能登录一个账号。现在授权中心多了 Antigravity 一组：点「用 Google 登录」或「添加账号」，在浏览器里添加账号，agy 里已经登录的账号也会自动收进来。

- **切换。** 在账号的菜单里选「切换 agy 到这个账号」，之后新开的 agy 都用这个号。原来登录的号会先收回授权中心，切走也不会丢。如果 agy 正在运行，会提醒你：已经打开的 agy 还用原来的号，而且可能把原来的号写回去，最好先退出。
- **每个账号的额度。** 每一行都显示自己的额度，不用切过去才能看。查额度只读额度，不调用模型。不能使用 Antigravity 的账号（比如有年龄限制的）会显示 Google 给出的原因，而不是一句看不懂的 403。
- **把官方卡绑定到账号。** 官方卡的表单里可以选一个账号：打开终端前会先把 agy 的登录切到这个号，已经是它就不再写入；卡片上显示的也是这个号的额度。不选就跟随 agy 当前的登录。卡片同步到另一台电脑后，那台电脑上也添加了这个号才能用，否则打开终端时会提示，不会用别的号启动。
- **删除账号不会让 agy 退出登录。** CC Switch 只删掉自己保存的那一份。

## 改进

**Windows 上的应用内更新不会再重启电脑**（[#8628](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8628)、[#8534](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8534)）。应用内更新以不弹对话框的方式运行 MSI 安装包，以前只要安装目录里有文件还被占用，Windows Installer 就会不提示直接重启电脑。现在安装包本身禁止重启，从旧版本更新到这一版时也生效。

**MSI 安装时可以不创建桌面快捷方式**（[#8601](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8601)、[#5667](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/5667)）。安装目录页多了「Create a desktop shortcut」选项，默认勾上；静默安装可以加 `CREATEDESKTOPSHORTCUT=0` 跳过。升级时保留现在的状态：你删掉的快捷方式不会被重新创建。桌面目录写不进去时也不会再让安装失败。

**页头显示实际的连接**（[#8634](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8634)）。实际连到哪里，从模式标签旁挪到应用名旁，用当前模式（直连、路由、聚合）的颜色画成一个小徽章；切到别的模式标签看时也一直显示，名称太长会截断，鼠标悬停可以看到全部。

**精简界面上的说明文字**（[#8633](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8633)）。供应商表单、OpenClaw、每日记忆、同步和整流器设置里，和旁边标签、标题重复的说明去掉了，补充说明挪进已有的帮助卡片；会影响结果的提示（费用、重启、同步、删除等）照常显示。

**用量页的应用筛选只列「应用」页里显示的应用。** 和会话管理一样：显示 Claude Desktop 时 Claude Code 也保留，当前选中的应用即使被隐藏也不会消失。

**预设：** 新增 DIT.ai、hao.ai。

## 修复

- **macOS 上并发请求多时路由失败**（[#8668](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8668)）。从访达或登录项启动的应用，同时能打开的文件数只有 256 个。路由每个进行中的请求要占一个客户端连接和一个上游连接，并发一多就用完了：接不了新请求、连不上上游，连配置文件和数据库都打不开。现在启动时把这个上限调高到系统允许的值（最多 10240）。Linux 同样处理。
- **从访达启动时，「重启 Codex 守护进程」报 `env: node: No such file or directory`**（[#8653](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8653)）。从访达启动时 CC Switch 只有系统目录的 PATH，npm 安装的 codex 要靠 node 运行，node 装在别的目录时就找不到。现在运行这类命令时会先加上登录 shell 的 PATH，和安装、升级工具时一样。OpenCode 获取模型列表也受这个问题影响，一并修复。
- **Claude Code 会话里用 `/cd` 换了目录，会话管理里仍归在旧项目下**（[#8643](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8643)、[#6862](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/6862)）。复制的恢复命令也会先 `cd` 到旧目录，在那里 `claude --resume` 找不到这个会话。现在和 Claude Code 自己的规则一样，按最后一次换到的目录归类，进出 worktree 也一样。
- **Windows 上打开终端后，按钮一直转圈，直到关掉那个终端窗口**（[#6712](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/6712)）。现在终端打开后就会结束等待。
- **Codex 没用过的额度窗口也显示重置倒计时**（[#8631](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8631)）。用量为 0 的窗口，Codex 返回的重置时间是「现在加一个窗口长度」，所以每次刷新倒计时都会跳回整个窗口（5 小时窗口跳回 5 小时）。现在用量为 0 的窗口不显示重置时间。
- **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 的请求显示「未定价」、按 0 元计。** OpenCode Go、OpenRouter 和 Hermes 预设用的模型名是 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`，以前价格表里没有。现在按 DeepSeek Flash 的官方价格计算；已经记录的请求不会重新计价。
- **手册里「官方额度用完后 Codex 锁住发送键」的绕开办法已失效，已更正**（[#7962](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7962)）。4.0.16 起聚合模式会保留 ChatGPT 登录，把第三方设为聚合的默认供应商已经绕不开。现在的办法是：切到直连，确认「设置 → 应用配置 → Codex」里的「非接管切换时保留官方登录」是关闭的，切到一家第三方供应商后彻底重启 Codex；额度重置后再切回聚合。

## 升级说明

**数据库版本从 20 升到 21**，为 MCP 和 Skills 增加 Antigravity 的开关。升级前会自动备份数据库；升级后再退回旧版本，旧版本会提示数据库版本过新，打不开。

- Antigravity 的供应商只在从卡片「使用此供应商打开终端」启动的 agy 里生效，在其他终端里直接运行 `agy` 不会用到它。
- Antigravity 默认显示在「应用」页，不用的话可以在那里隐藏。
- 在授权中心管理 Antigravity 账号目前只支持 macOS。其他平台不显示账号选择，官方卡跟随 agy 自己的登录；从 Mac 同步过来的绑定会被忽略。

---

## 致谢

感谢 @Owlbay、@peterLwk888、@ajia1206（Antigravity CLI 支持）、@YUZHEthefool（Windows 更新不再重启、可选桌面快捷方式）、@funkpopo（可选桌面快捷方式）、@SaladDay（页头连接徽章、精简说明文字）、@Dopetaiga（`/cd` 后的会话归类）、@cuiyf5516（Codex 未使用的额度窗口）、@umutcankurt（Windows 打开终端一直等待）的贡献。

感谢 @lm902、@zhufeizzz、@AisinGioroKiIoi、@WzLYVg387U、@mvdorofeev、@dw2286、@LeenixP 报告问题、提供复现信息和修复思路。

完整的技术细节请见 [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)。

name: v0.11.0
body:
The latest release of Lore, Epic Games' next-generation open source version control system.

[Quickstart](https://epicgames.github.io/lore/tutorials/quickstart/) | [Design](https://epicgames.github.io/lore/explanation/system-design/) | [Documentation](https://epicgames.github.io/lore/) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/E4SFJKRPbg)

## Quick Install

Windows
```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EpicGames/lore/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

macOS / Linux
```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EpicGames/lore/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

## Release Notes

Changes since v0.10.1.

### Breaking changes

- C API: the new `LORE_EVENT_FILE_AUDIT` event adds a member to `lore_event_t`; rebuild against the new `lore.h`
- `[environment.endpoint] user_url` now names a `lore.user.v1.UserService` (`UserGet`, `UserFind`) instead of the `UrcAuthApi` `GetUserInfo` / `GetUserId` calls. With `user_url` set, the server also lists repositories there by default (`[server.auth] repository_catalog = "user_service"`) and registers the repositories it creates and deletes there instead of calling `RebacApi`. Without it, clients ask `auth_url` as before
- A client and the Lore service it relays to must come from the same build (message protocol version 2); restart the service after upgrading
- Data is verified by the trust of its source ([ADR-00023](https://github.com/EpicGames/lore/blob/main/docs/developing/decisions/00023-data-verification-and-trust.md)): local store reads no longer verify hashes, and data fetched from a remote is verified on receipt unless the remote is trusted (`--trust-remote`). C API: `skip_verify` on `lore_storage_open_args_t` is now an alias of `trust_remote` and skips verifying fetched data only
- C API: `lore_branch_merge_start_args_t` gains `link_paths` and `link_messages`, changing its size; rebuild against the new `lore.h`. A zero-initialized struct keeps today's behavior
- `lore-server`: refuses to start if `[server.auth] resource_id_template` or `[server.auth.oidc]` `resource_template` / `scope_template` lacks `{id}`, since such a template let one grant match every partition

### Features

- `lore file audit <path>` shows, for each line of a file, the revision that last changed it, grouped into ranges of consecutive lines (C API: `lore_file_audit` / `lore_file_audit_async`)
- `--trust-remote` (C API: `trust_remote` on `lore_global_args_t`) skips hash verification of fetched data, keeping only a size check, for machines inside the remote's own infrastructure such as build servers. C callers must zero the whole struct, padding included, or stray bytes turn it on
- C API: `fragments` on `lore_storage_get_resolved_item_t` delivers content piece by piece as stored (`LORE_EVENT_STORAGE_GET_FRAGMENT`), leaving decoding and verification to the reader, which can keep payloads compressed
- `lore auth login` against an OIDC issuer uses the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (RFC 8628), opening the verification URL in the browser or printing it with `--no-browser`; `--token-type <TYPE> --token <TOKEN>` logs in with an existing token through RFC 8693 token exchange. Partition and repository operations send the access token, or a per-partition token when the server advertises `resource_template` / `scope_template`. ID tokens are never stored or sent; refresh and client credentials grants aren't implemented yet
- The user identity is read from a token by the same rule on client and server: the `identity` claim (or `https://lore.org/claims/identity`), else `sub`. Tokens with an empty or non-string identity are refused, and `[server.auth] identity_claim` is removed
- `lore branch merge` and `lore branch merge start` take `--link-message <PATH> <MESSAGE>`, as `lore commit` does
- `lore clone --offline` / `--cache` prepares a clone so staging and committing work without a connection
- `lore service status` reports the status of the running Lore service
- `LORE_STORE_RETAIN=1` keeps a process's stores loaded between repository calls, without holding their locks, for `store_keep_alive_seconds` (default 10). While it's set, don't share a store directory with processes of an earlier build
- `lore-server`: `[server.http] health_only = true` serves only `/health_check`
- `lore-server` metrics: gRPC requests record `rpc.server.handler.duration`, excluding request upload and pre-body work such as authorization, and `BranchPush` records its fragment verification load under `lore.branch_push`
- `contrib/bazel/`: a Bazel remote execution server (Remote Execution API v2) keeping its action cache and content-addressable storage in Lore partitions

### Fixes & Improvements

- `lore sync --reset` replaces a directory with a file at the same path instead of failing with "Is a directory", and syncs, branch switches, resets, merges and view changes report each deleted file and directory via `LORE_EVENT_REVISION_SYNC_FILE`. Files and directories named `.urc` or `.lore`, in any case, are ignored by every command
- `lore commit` and `lore clone` report the error that stopped them instead of `Recursion task failed`, and a failed clone no longer prints `Clone complete` (C API: `LORE_EVENT_REPOSITORY_CLONE_END` is sent only on success)
- `lore status`: `--scan` of many paths runs in parallel, files are listed in stable path order, and modified files are no longer missed after a scan that dropped a reverted add or after a same-size re-save
- Merges of divergent history (such as a sync with new local and remote revisions): `lore file history` attributes remote changes correctly, remote additions and earlier remote changes are kept, committing no longer fails in some cases, and the branch is reported ahead of the remote instead of diverged afterwards
- Layers: committing a staged layer works when the parent tree holds only unstaged dirty changes, and several commands no longer copy the current revision's metadata, such as its reviewer, onto the next revision
- Merge conflicts: a branch's change to a file is no longer dropped without a conflict in some add-after-delete cases, and resolving to one side no longer uses memory in proportion to the size of the tree
- Links: committing through a link pinned at a merge revision no longer records a spurious merge, staging inside a nested link more than once no longer pushes intermediate states, and `lore commit --link-message` accepts any spelling of the link path
- `lore dirty` inside a link, or on its mount, marks the change in the linked repository, so `lore status` and staging pick it up without a scan
- Lore service: commands run with the caller's configuration and credentials, `lore_storage_put` / `lore_storage_get` (and their `_resolved` variants) work through the service, unreadable shared stores or instances are skipped at startup, and on Linux and macOS two services started at once no longer both run
- Auth: the CLI sends tokens only to hosts named in their `root_domains` or `aud` claims, no longer to the `iss` host except for token exchange. With `[server.auth] resource_claim` set, repository lookups by name or id answer any verified caller, so clone, `lore link add`, `lore layer add`, `repository info` and `repository delete` no longer fail as not found before the caller holds a grant
- Server write checks: pushing to a protected branch requires the `push-protected` action and the `is_service_account` claim no longer bypasses protection, so grant `push-protected` to mirroring accounts first. Generic `MutableStore` / `MutableCompareAndSwap` requests can no longer write repository metadata, branch metadata or branch latest pointers; use `RepositoryMetadataSet`, `BranchMetadataSet` and `BranchPush`
- `RevisionList`: listing from a revision above the branch's latest no longer crashes the server, and paging through older history on a deep branch no longer times out with `Cancelled`
- Pushing and committing: some large files no longer fail to commit or push, and a retried push or a gRPC push copying the same content to several files no longer fails with a missing fragment
- Verification: caches, prefetches and immutable store queries verify fetched data unless the remote is trusted, fetching again once after asking the server to repair it, and corrupt local data is fetched again and replaced instead of crashing an unverified read
- Reads: streaming reads and reads into files enforce the content size limit, a corrupt fragment list with out-of-order offsets fails the read instead of returning wrong data, and reads of fragmented content do less redundant work
- Fetching: concurrent reads of the same missing content download it once, and caching runs at most 512 fetches at once per remote connection (`LORE_CACHE_GETS`), so reads a command needs right away don't queue behind it
- `lore-server` with a `remote` store verifies data fetched from the backend and asks it to repair failures, refuses data in a codec it's built without (such as Oodle), size-checks data from replicas and peers, and no longer crashes on a truncated replica response
- Oodle: the local store's Oodle migration finishes sooner, and a build without Oodle replaces such data with the remote's re-encoded copy, or reports `NotSupported` where there's no remote copy
- Commands start faster, as opening a repository lists each store's index once; `lore repository create` syncs to disk only with `--sync-data`
- Fix a deadlock between processes using one repository, such as the Lore service and a storage handle; stores are now locked only while in use, so idle handles no longer block other processes
- Local store durability: transient I/O errors, failed or interrupted flushes, obliterates and index reorganizations no longer lose data, bring back removed entries or serve another file's data, and background index flushes now follow every change
- A local store whose `version` file can't be read fails to open instead of re-migrating on every open; an affected store recovers at its next command connected to the remote
- Obliterate in local stores is saved to disk before the data is zeroed and waits for reads in progress, and obliterated content no longer comes back when stored again under another context or re-encoded
- Compaction does far less disk work and no longer stalls server stores for minutes; client stores never evict local-only data, and `lore repository gc` no longer swaps `max_size` and `max_capacity`
- Storage sessions: handles reuse one server session per partition, so long-running processes are no longer refused every later call, and an unauthorized session is retried once with fresh authorization
- Reconnects: storage handles and servers' remote stores reconnect after a failed connection, with a backoff of up to 30 seconds, QUIC streams that stop carrying requests reconnect instead of hanging, and reads and uploads use all the connections `--max-connections` allows
- QUIC: the vendored `quinn-proto` moves to 0.11.19, fixing CVE-2026-25800 (unauthenticated remote memory exhaustion) and other upstream memory-exhaustion, stream-limit, Retry-token and path MTU issues
- QUIC throughput: congestion control and stream ordering fixes, and the client asks for a larger UDP receive buffer; on Linux, set `net.core.rmem_max` to `524288` or more to allow it
- C API: a call reading into `data_out` that stops part way no longer writes the caller's buffer after completion. `data_out` must stay valid until completion, and `lore_shutdown` is safe only once every call has completed

## Release Assets

> [!IMPORTANT]
These can be downloaded under the "Assets" section below.

### Installer
- `lore-setup` - Lore CLI Windows installer

### Binaries
- `lore` - Lore CLI
- `loreserver` - Lore Server
- `liblore` - Lore Shared Library

### Headers
- `lore.h` - Single header for `liblore` (packged with `liblore`)

### Supported Platforms
- Windows x84_64
- macOS AArch64
- Linux x86_64
- Linux AArch64 (for Graviton/Neoverse 512-tvb only)

## Lore Desktop Client

> [!IMPORTANT]
Lore Desktop Client is available as binaries only, download the installer for your platform here:

- Windows: [Lore-Desktop-Setup-x64.exe](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/Lore-Desktop-Setup-x64.exe)
- macOS: [Lore-Desktop-arm64.dmg](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/Lore-Desktop-arm64.dmg)
- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04): [lore-desktop_amd64.deb](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/lore-desktop_amd64.deb)
- Linux (AppImage): [Lore-Desktop-x86_64.AppImage](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/Lore-Desktop-x86_64.AppImage)

##  ⬇️ Open Source Lore Assets Below ⬇️

name: Niubash v1.4.4
body:
Niubash v1.4.4 packages for Windows, Linux, and macOS.

Engine: rubash git fa64d58dfb9c — every platform build in this release compiled that same revision, pinned by `scripts/release/rubash-pin.json` and fail-hard verified at fetch time (rubash#827). The release compiles the pinned engine, not "whatever rubash master was when the pipeline ran".
Verify locally with `niu --version`, which prints the same revision.

Windows (x64, ARM64): Inno Setup installers (`*-setup.exe`) add user PATH and Windows Terminal profile integration; portable archives bundle `niu` with WinuxCmd and bash/sh shims.

Portable download guide (niubash#470): prefer `*.tar.gz` — it is hardlink-native. The bundled payload ships real NTFS hardlinks (the whole `git.exe` family is one shared binary, `awk`/`gawk` likewise, exactly what `wpm install` lays down), so the tarball is roughly half the zip's download size and unpacks to a much smaller on-disk tree; `tar -xf <file>.tar.gz` works out of the box on Windows 10 1803+ and any modern Linux/macOS, and on a filesystem without hardlink support (FAT32/exFAT) extraction degrades gracefully to independent byte-identical copies with no loss of function. `*.7z` is the smallest download (solid LZMA already collapses the shared payloads) but current 7-Zip releases restore the shared families as independent copies — every file is byte-identical, only disk usage grows. The classic `*.zip` is unchanged, stores every payload in full, and remains for tooling that only speaks zip.

Windows packages come with the must-install bundle pre-installed (niubash#189, niubash#209): niugit (native Windows git — the full plugin distro's five entries install through git, so a fresh machine without git.exe no longer fails `niu setup`), gawk 5.4.1 with plain `awk` working too, plus ripgrep (`rg`) and fd — all landing in the bundled WinuxCmd root as wpm JSON-package payloads, assembled at CI time with no runtime downloads, no runtime archive formats, and no symlinks. Pre-install is best-effort, not a promise: on legs where the package index has no matching artifact (currently niugit and gawk on the ARM64 builds; ripgrep and fd have ARM64 artifacts) the package ships WITHOUT that entry — run `winuxcmd wpm install <name>` once after installing to add it. The pre-install list and its recorded exclusions live in `scripts/release/preinstall.json`.

`niubash-skill-v<version>.zip` is the AI agent skill bundle (SKILL.md + references, WinuxCmd-skill layout): unpack it into an agent skills directory, or let the shell do it — `niu skill install` embeds the same content.

Linux (x86_64, aarch64; glibc): portable tarballs with the `niu` binary, README, and LICENSE — Unix builds bundle nothing, native system tools are used. Untar anywhere and run `./niu`.

macOS (aarch64, x86_64): portable tarballs with the `niu` binary, README, and LICENSE. Untar anywhere and run `./niu`.

Every artifact was smoke-verified on the build OS of the job that produced it, before upload: `niu -c 'echo ok'`, `printf 'a\nb\n' | niu -c 'sort | head -1'`, an offline `NIU_PLUGIN_SPEC=<empty> niu plugin sync --bootstrap` (exit 0, no output, no network), and a `niu --version` check against this tag and the engine revision.

Integrity (niubash#311): `SHA256SUMS` lists the SHA-256 of every shipped artifact, and each Windows installer has a `.sha256` sidecar beside it. `niu --self-update` verifies the installer against the sidecar before running it and aborts rather than execute anything it cannot verify. The same digests feed the winget manifest `InstallerSha256`.


## What's Changed
* fix(release): emit version in publish-crates resolve step so the crates guard can compare by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/494
* docs(readme): overhaul — evidence-pinned Performance section, Android baseline, gate receipts by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/493
* docs(pages): refresh site for v1.4.3 — 24-agent roster, generated loader, pinned perf numbers by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/496
* docs(skill): refresh agent skill bundle for the 1.4.3 surface by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/498
* feat(msix): Microsoft Store readiness — writable LocalCache root, link family, Store self-update, WT fragments by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/497
* fix(console): probe winuxcmd on PATH without spawning where.exe; pin test to v1.1.19 by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/506
* docs(rc): rewrite .niubashrc.example to the manifest+loader model by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/500
* docs(site): winget install, Android shipped, encoded-command handoff by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/502
* docs: winget quickstart + Android platform status matches reality by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/501
* chore(release): re-pin bundled WinuxCmd to v1.1.20 by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/507


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/compare/v1.4.3...v1.4.4

name: GitHub CLI 2.103.0
body:
## Expiring, auto-refreshing OAuth tokens (preview)

`gh` can now sign in with expiring OAuth credentials that it refreshes automatically. When you opt in, `gh` stores a short-lived access token alongside a rotating refresh token and refreshes the access token whenever it is needed, so you stay signed in without having to authenticate again.

To opt in for a single sign-in, run:

```shell
gh auth login --expiring
```

To prefer expiring credentials for every sign-in, run:

```shell
gh config set expiring_credentials enabled
```

`gh auth status` shows whether a credential is refreshable and when the current access token expires. Both `gh auth status` and `gh auth token` automatically refresh the access token when needed. Expiring tokens are available on github.com and GHE.com; on hosts that do not issue them, `gh` falls back to a regular non-expiring token.

If you use HTTPS as your git protocol, we advise using git 2.46 or newer and letting `gh` act as your git credential helper by running `gh auth setup-git`. This way `gh` serves and refreshes the expiring credential for git, and git does not cache it past its lifetime.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Expiring access tokens should not be cached. Scripts and extensions that store the output of `gh auth token` will eventually hold an expired token, so run `gh auth token` again each time a token is needed. Tokens supplied through `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` are never refreshed.

For more information, see [Authenticating with GitHub CLI](https://docs.github.com/github-cli/github-cli/authenticating-with-github-cli#using-expiring-refreshable-tokens).

## Manage issue artifacts with `gh issue artifact` (private preview)

`gh issue artifact` brings issue artifacts to the command line. Users and organizations enrolled in the private preview can use the `list`, `view`, `create`, `edit`, `download`, and `delete` commands to manage issue artifacts.

```shell
# Create a Markdown document with an attached image
gh issue artifact create 142 signin-plan.md --attach ./signin-flow.png

# Create an HTML document
gh issue artifact create 142 menu-prototype.html

# List or view artifacts
gh issue artifact list 142
gh issue artifact view 142 2

# Update a document or restore an earlier version
gh issue artifact edit 142 2 --body-file signin-plan-v2.md
gh issue artifact edit 142 2 --restore-version 5
```

Artifacts can also be addressed by their GitHub URLs, and Markdown documents support image and video attachments with `--attach`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Issue artifacts are in private preview. These commands only work for repositories enrolled in the preview. See the [Issue Artifacts private preview announcement and feedback discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/205881) for access instructions and to share feedback.

## Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-21.

Following [uv 0.13.4](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/tag/0.13.4), which removed the affected eMudhra/emSign root from uv's own certificate store, this release updates the latest managed CPython builds for 3.11 and newer to [python-build-standalone 20261021](https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/tag/20261021), including the CPython [3.15.1](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3151/), [3.14.9](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3149/), and [3.13.17](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31317/) security patch releases. These builds include [pip 26.2.2](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/news/#v26-2-2) both preinstalled in the managed interpreter and bundled with `ensurepip`, which installs pip by default when you run `python -m venv`. Both copies use certifi 2026.10.19, which removes the same affected root. After upgrading uv, run `uv python upgrade` to install the updated builds. Virtual environments pinned to an older Python patch version do not switch to the updated interpreter automatically. Upgrade pip separately in existing virtual environments.

Please note upstream CPython 3.9 and 3.10 still bundle pip releases whose certificate bundles trust the affected eMudhra/emSign root. We recommend migrating off of those versions and will no longer be releasing Docker images with uv installed for EOL Python versions.

### Enhancements

- Report incompatible self-dependencies directly in resolution errors ([#21845](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21845))

### Python

- Add CPython 3.15.1, 3.14.9, and 3.13.17 ([#22802](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22802))

### Preview features

- Select and rank wheel variants with no required properties or properties from PEP 850 static providers in platform-specific resolutions with `wheel-variants` ([#22535](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22535), [#22536](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22536), [#22687](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22687), [#22688](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22688))

### Performance

- Reduce peak memory use when resolving dependencies across multiple environments ([#22769](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22769), [#22770](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22770), [#22784](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22784))
- Speed up exports with complex transitive extras by resolving activation across the dependency graph ([#22751](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22751))
- Reduce uv's binary size by keeping additional error formatters out of line ([#22775](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22775))
- Reduce overhead when parsing custom build cache keys ([#22749](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22749))

### Bug fixes

- Lock packages distributed only as Android wheels without a source distribution ([#22806](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22806))
- Export optional dependencies correctly when transitive extras are activated through different or incompatible environment paths ([#22751](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22751))
- Reject invalid custom build cache keys instead of silently falling back to the defaults ([#22749](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22749))

### Security

- Reject certificate chains containing compromised eMudhra intermediate keys via `rustls-webpki` 0.103.16 ([#22777](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22777))
- Stop publishing uv Docker images based on Python 3.9 and 3.10 images that no longer receive upstream updates ([#22773](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22773))

## Verifying GitHub Artifact Attestations

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify):
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --repo astral-sh/uv
```

You can also download the attestation from [GitHub](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/attestations) and verify against that directly:
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --bundle <file-path of downloaded attestation>
```

# OpenWhispr 1.10.4

Tone & Style writes your dictation, and the assistant's drafts, in the tone you pick for each kind of app. The AI Summary is more detailed by default, notes can link to a calendar event, and you can set a reasoning effort per model scope.

## 🌟 Highlights

- **🎨 Tone & Style** — Pick a tone for personal messages, work chats, email and everything else, and cleanup writes in it for the app you're in. Off by default; turn it on in Settings → Tone & Style.
- **📝 Detailed AI Summary** — Generate AI Summary now writes the same notes as the Detailed Notes template.
- **📅 Calendar events on notes** — Link any note to its meeting to pull in the guests and join link.
- **🧠 Reasoning effort** — Choose how hard reasoning models think, per scope.
- **❓ Ask about OpenWhispr** — The chat answers questions about the app from the docs and your settings.

## ✨ Also new

"This is me" in the speaker picker, searchable overflow for long sidebar folders, onboarding key checks as you type, Claude 5.5 models, and Qwen3.8 27B on Groq.

## 🛠 Fixes

- **Dictation:** Local and self-hosted cleanup models always run when you dictate through OpenWhispr Cloud or a streaming provider, and a failed selection edit keeps your transcript.
- **Meetings and notes:** Resumed recordings keep speakers apart, stopping a local meeting keeps its last words, and in-person speakers are no longer all attributed to you.
- **Transcription and AI:** OpenAI live dictation uses your language and dictionary, stalled replies no longer hang, and self-hosted models stay selected after a restart.
- **Linux:** Voice assistant answers paste at the caret, and paste works on niri, sway, Hyprland and KDE with non-Latin layouts.
- **Windows:** Local Whisper works for user profiles with accented names.

## ⚠️ Heads-up

On niri, sway and Hyprland, auto-paste into Wayland apps now needs `wl-clipboard`.

Full details in the [changelog](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#1104---2026-10-21).

## 🙏 Thanks

Thanks to @Chadpiha, @boseq, @greatcoat, @hsusul, @IdrisGit, @clarkmaan, @Nathan-Roll1, @Adityakk9031, @etzelm, @widechaos, @Jrjy3, @jay-tau, @agn-7, @matthias-vera, @Abhishek-B-R, @atty57, @ivaschru, @isacgalvao, @tishmen, @Li-john1021 and @Sevi-py, and to @PalaceChan and @mhasgari for their bug reports. 🎉

name: 1.4 Short Circuit
body:
# Resume Matcher 1.4: Short Circuit

Short Circuit makes the resume itself better, not only better matched. Every tailoring run now critiques its own writing and rewrites the weak lines without adding a single fact, you can push a missing job keyword in when you confirm you have it, and you can watch each stage of the work as it happens. It also brings agent mode, an MCP server, new templates and multi-page resumes, and a round of security hardening.

Named after **Short Circuit** from Daft Punk's *Discovery*, this release continues the v1 series after **1.3 Crescendolls**.

## What's new

### Writing that holds up

- **Critique and rewrite in every tailoring run.** Fixed rules and an AI critic check each bullet and the summary. Lines with an em dash, a weak opener such as "Responsible for", or no stated outcome get one rewrite. A fact check drops any rewrite that adds or loses a number, name, tool or skill, so your work stays on the page and nothing is invented. Light nudge only critiques.
- **Writing score.** A 0 to 100 score from the fixed rules (the same with every AI provider), with before and after, the lines to fix and the reviewer's notes.
- **Improve writing in the Builder.** A new Writing tab scores any resume, master included, and rewrites its weak lines. You review every change before it goes into the editor.
- **Heavy rewrite.** A fourth tailoring mode for bigger edits: full Challenge, Action, Result rewrites, a new summary and reordered bullets, with a clear hallucination warning.
- **Evidence-based cover letters.** One page, usually 200 to 300 words: a hook tied to the job, two or three matching examples, a company-fit paragraph grounded in the job description and a specific close. Contributed by @AlexanderMorris2k.

### Keywords on your terms

- **Add missing keywords.** In the review dialog, missing job keywords become chips. Keywords your master shows are applied directly; a keyword it does not show needs your "I have this". Each one goes into your skills plus at most two lines where it fits, and nothing else is added around it.
- **See where they went.** The dialog lists where every keyword landed, marks it in the changed lines and shows the ATS score before and after. JD Match highlights the keywords you added in blue, and interview prep asks about them first.
- **One match number.** JD Match now shows the same keyword match as the ATS score, and keeps C++, .NET, Node.js and CI/CD whole.
- **A sharper ATS score.** It now scores the job title and date consistency, and the builder keeps the last calculated score with a Recalculate button. Contributed by @himalyansailor.
- **ATS parse check.** A new ATS CHECK tab shows whether a plain text extractor can read your exported PDF in the right order.

### Watch it work

- **Live progress.** Tailoring shows each real stage as it runs, with a note when a slow model needs a minute.
- **Tailoring queue.** Queue several job descriptions and tailor them one after another, with cooldowns that respect rate limits. Contributed by @coolb0y.

### Use it your way

- **Agent mode.** Open Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot or Antigravity in the repo and ask it to tailor your resume: no API key, and the web app updates live as the agent saves.
- **MCP server.** Its tools let any MCP client drive Resume Matcher against the same database as the app. Contributed by @rrvrs.
- **Claude Code and ChatGPT plans as providers.** Run on a Claude Code install with no API key (contributed by @GongYuanCaiJi), pick its model, or sign in with a ChatGPT plan, with a clear note on subscription risk.
- **Optional PostgreSQL** for larger or shared setups.

### More control over the resume

- **Several master resumes.** Keep up to five, one per career track; tailoring picks the strongest bullets with code, not the AI.
- **Page limit and bullet cap** settings for tailoring. Contributed by @himalyansailor.
- **New templates:** Deedy, Modern Deedy and Vivid Single Column, plus multi-page resumes with predictable page breaks and an academic CV mode.
- **The PDF matches the preview,** and each resume keeps its own formatting.
- **Reorder everything:** projects, custom section items (contributed by @Bdysj) and the bullets within an entry.

## Security

- **Saved API keys can no longer be sent to arbitrary servers** ([#1045](https://github.com/srbhr/Resume-Matcher/pull/1045), reported and fixed by @MahediBuilds). An unauthenticated caller could point a stored key at their own server; a saved custom Base URL is now bound to the key that confirmed it.
- **Local by default** ([#1048](https://github.com/srbhr/Resume-Matcher/pull/1048)). The app has no login, so it now listens on loopback only and rejects unexpected `Host` headers.
- **LiteLLM.** Resume Matcher pins `litellm==1.104.2` and was not affected by the compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release of 2026-10-21. Keep that pin in mind before upgrading LiteLLM.
- Dependency updates: cryptography 50.0.0, Next.js 16.3.3, DOMPurify 3.4.13, undici 7.30.0, sharp 0.35.4, js-yaml 4.3.2 and Vitest.

## Upgrading from 1.3

**Back up the complete data directory first**, as always: the database, `config.json`, uploaded files and the hidden `.secret_key` together.

- **The app now listens on `127.0.0.1` only.** If you open it from another machine or a reverse proxy, set `BIND_ADDRESS` (Docker Compose) or `HOST` (source installs) and add the host name to `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, for example `BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 ALLOWED_HOSTS=192.168.1.20 docker compose up -d`. See [SETUP.md](https://github.com/srbhr/Resume-Matcher/blob/main/SETUP.md) for details.
- **Database changes are additive** and run on startup: new columns for ATS scores, per-resume formatting and forced keywords.
- Source installs still need **Node.js 22+** and **Python 3.13+**; reinstall dependencies after pulling.

## Docker images

Release tag: **`v1.4.0`**. Versioned images for Linux **amd64** and **arm64** publish to GHCR and Docker Hub:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/srbhr/resume-matcher:1.4.0
# or
docker pull srbhr/resume-matcher:1.4.0
```

The image tags are `1.4.0` and `1.4`.

## Verification

The release passed **1,944 backend tests** and **1,596 frontend tests** with type checking. The writing loop, live progress and keyword forcing were also run end to end against a real model through the app's proxy.

## Thank you

Thank you to everyone who contributed code, reported bugs on Discord and GitHub, tested fixes and reviewed this release.

**Contributors to this release:** @576657922, @AlexanderMorris2k, @Bdysj, @coolb0y, @Frankli9986, @gingeekrishna, @GongYuanCaiJi, @himalyansailor, @HT-Moh, @kobihikri, @MahediBuilds, @rrvrs, @srbhr.

Automation contributions are credited to @dependabot.
